breakfast.name: Pan con Tomate
instructions: Pan con tomate (Catalan: pa amb tomaquet) is the Catalan breakfast ritual
Toast the bread until golden and slightly crispy
Rub raw garlic once, lightly -- a background note
Rub the cut tomato face directly onto the bread -- the flesh smears in
Drizzle olive oil generously -- it soaks in after the tomato
Season with flaky salt
Pa amb tomaquet is eaten every morning in Catalonia
Topped with iberico ham, anchovies, or eaten plain -- all versions correct
breakfast.description: The Catalan morning ritual -- crusty bread rubbed with raw garlic and the face of a very ripe tomato until the flesh smears into the toast, soaked with good olive oil and flaky salt. Simple but requires quality: very ripe tomato, very good oil. Eaten every morning in Catalonia; topped with jamon or anchovies or plain.

breakfast.name: Churros con Chocolate
ingredients: Churros dough: water, flour, salt (piped and fried)
Chocolate a la taza: dark chocolate, whole milk, cornstarch (very thick)
instructions: Churros con chocolate is the Spanish ceremonial breakfast
The chocolate a la taza is thick, almost pudding -- cornstarch thickens it
Fry churros until golden-crispy outside, still slightly soft inside
Roll fried churros in granulated sugar immediately
Dip the churro into thick chocolate -- the chocolate clings to sugar-coated churro
Churrerias open at midnight for post-clubbing churros -- the 3am ritual
Churros con chocolate for New Year: many families end New Year night with churros
breakfast.description: Spain ceremonial breakfast and midnight post-party ritual -- fried dough sticks rolled in sugar and dipped in thick hot chocolate (so thick with cornstarch it is almost pudding). The churreria is a social institution. New Year midnight, post-clubbing 3am, cold winter mornings: churros appear at all three.

breakfast.name: Tortilla Espanola
ingredients: Olive oil (enough to submerge the potatoes)
instructions: Tortilla espanola is the Spanish national dish
The debate: onion or no onion? -- Spain has been divided for generations
The potatoes must be COOKED in olive oil until very soft -- not fried crispy
The olive oil potato confit: barely bubbling in oil until tender and sweet
Drain the oil, mix potatoes with beaten eggs -- let them sit and absorb
The flip: plate over the pan, invert, slide back
Tortilla should be slightly runny in the center (jugosa) -- not dry
Dry tortilla is considered a failure in Spain
Eaten at any time: breakfast, in a bocadillo for lunch, tapas at night
breakfast.description: The Spanish national egg dish -- potatoes confited in olive oil until soft and sweet, mixed with beaten eggs, cooked and flipped via a plate inversion. The center must be jugosa (runny-creamy), never dry. The onion vs no onion debate has divided Spain for generations. Eaten as breakfast, in a bocadillo for lunch, or as tapas at night.

breakfast.name: Migas (Fried Breadcrumbs)
instructions: Migas are the Castilian and Extremaduran peasant breakfast
Stale bread crumbled into irregular pieces -- moisture added overnight
The bread needs to be slightly damp before frying -- prevents burning
Fry in generous olive oil or lard with garlic -- the garlic infuses the fat
Add smoked paprika -- the red oil colors the migas orange-red
Fry slowly, stirring constantly, until golden and crunchy
The chorizo or tocino fried alongside in the same pan
Serve with fresh grapes -- sweetness against savory fried bread
breakfast.description: Castilian shepherd breakfast -- stale bread crumbled and fried in olive oil with garlic and smoked paprika until golden-crunchy, served with fried chorizo and fresh grapes. The grapes against the garlicky, paprika-red fried bread is the elevation. Uses old bread; nothing wasted.

lunch.name: Gazpacho Andaluz
instructions: Gazpacho is the cold soup of Andalusia -- the hottest region of Europe
Ripe tomatoes are the soul -- underripe tomatoes produce inferior gazpacho
The bread: soaked and blended in -- it thickens the soup
The olive oil: blended in slowly to emulsify -- makes the soup silky
The red wine vinegar: brightens all flavors
Blend smooth, pass through sieve for silky texture
Serve very cold -- the temperature matters as much as the flavor
Salmorejo is the thicker Cordoba version -- more bread, topped with egg and ham
lunch.description: Andalusian cold tomato soup -- very ripe tomatoes blended with cucumber, pepper, garlic, stale bread, red wine vinegar, and olive oil emulsified into a silky chilled soup. Served ice cold. Andalusia is the hottest region of Europe. Salmorejo (Cordoba) is the thicker, creamier cousin.

lunch.name: Cocido Madrileno
instructions: Cocido madrileno is the Madrid Sunday lunch -- the quintessential Castilian stew
Served in three courses (vuelcos): first the broth with fideos noodles
Second course: the chickpeas and vegetables
Third course: the meats (beef, chorizo, morcilla, tocino)
The chickpeas soaked overnight -- they go in with cold water and meat
Saffron gives golden color to the broth
All components cook together in one pot
The morcilla (blood sausage) is the most distinctive element
lunch.description: Madrid Sunday lunch served in three courses (vuelcos) -- first broth with fideos noodles, then chickpeas and vegetables, then the meats (beef, chorizo, morcilla blood sausage, tocino). All cooked together in one pot. Takes all morning. The morcilla is the most distinctive element.

lunch.name: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Paella valenciana is the original paella -- NOT seafood, NOT mixed
Paella is Valencian -- from the Albufera area, the Valencia rice fields
The authentic version: chicken, rabbit, flat beans, green beans -- NO seafood
Adding seafood to a valenciana is considered wrong in Valencia
The paellera (wide, shallow pan) creates the socarrat
The socarrat: the crispy caramelized rice crust on the bottom
Once the broth is added, NEVER STIR
Paella cooked over orange wood fire in Valencia -- the smoke adds flavor
lunch.description: The original paella from Albufera, Valencia -- chicken, rabbit, flat garrofon beans, and green beans in saffron-yellow short-grain rice with a socarrat (caramelized crispy rice crust). NO seafood: adding seafood to a valenciana is considered wrong in Valencia. Never stir once broth is added. Cooked over orange wood fire outdoors on Sundays.

lunch.name: Fabada Asturiana
ingredients: Fabe de la Granja beans (large white Asturian beans -- soaked overnight)
instructions: Fabada asturiana is the definitive Asturian dish
Asturias: the green, rainy, mountain-and-sea region of northern Spain
The fabe de la Granja bean: large, creamy white, grown only in Asturias
The compango: the meats (morcilla, chorizo, tocino, lacon) that cook with the beans
Everything in a single pot -- water covers everything
The key technique: a very gentle simmer, never boiling
Hard boiling breaks the beans -- gentle simmer keeps them whole but creamy inside
The fat from the compango emulsifies with the bean broth
Paired with Asturian cider poured from height
lunch.description: Asturian cold-weather bean stew -- large fabe de la Granja beans cooked at a very gentle simmer with morcilla, chorizo, tocino, and lacon (the compango) until the fat emulsifies into a rich, creamy broth. Never boil: hard boiling breaks the beans. Paired with Asturian cider poured from height.

lunch.name: Pulpo a la Gallega
instructions: Pulpo a la gallega (pulpo a feira) is the Galician octopus dish
Galicia: the Atlantic coast of northwestern Spain
The octopus is tenderized by freezing overnight then boiling
Traditional technique: dip the octopus three times in boiling water before submerging
Boil until tender: 45-60 minutes depending on size
Slice on a wooden board -- traditional in Galicia
Serve on wooden plate with boiled potatoes as base
Generous olive oil poured over, then flaky salt, then smoked paprika
lunch.description: Galician octopus -- whole octopus frozen overnight (to tenderize), dipped three times in boiling water (traditional technique), boiled 45-60 minutes, sliced on a wooden board, served over boiled potatoes with olive oil, flaky salt, and smoked paprika. Served on wooden plates at Galician markets and festivals.

dinner.name: Pintxos (Basque Bar Snacks)
instructions: Pintxos are Basque bar snacks -- the San Sebastian evening ritual
The Basque Country has the highest Michelin star concentration per capita in the world
The pintxo: small piece of bread topped with combinations of ingredients on a stick
Bars in San Sebastian Old Town compete fiercely for the best pintxos
The pintxo bar ritual: walk from bar to bar, one glass of txakoli wine, one pintxo, move on
Txakoli: the sharp, slightly sparkling Basque white wine -- poured from height
Gilda: the classic pintxo -- anchovy, olive, pickled pepper on a stick -- from the 1940s
dinner.description: Basque bar snack and San Sebastian evening ritual -- small pieces of crusty bread topped with anchovy, ham, cheese, pickled peppers, and hard-boiled egg, held by cocktail sticks. The ritual: walk from bar to bar, one txakoli wine, one pintxo, move on. The Gilda (anchovy + olive + pickled pepper) is the original from the 1940s.

dinner.name: Jamon Iberico
ingredients: Jamon iberico de bellota (acorn-fed, highest grade)
instructions: Jamon iberico is the crown of Spanish cured meats
The Iberian pig: a specific breed that infiltrates fat into muscle
The de bellota designation: the pig feeds exclusively on acorns in the dehesa
The dehesa: the cork and holm oak ecosystem of Extremadura and western Andalusia
Acorn diet gives the ham a nutty, complex fat -- the fat is the quality marker
Curing process: salted, dried, aged in mountain air for 36-48 months minimum
The fat melts at room temperature -- served at room temp, never cold
Cut by hand on a jamon stand (jamonero) -- the knife skill is a craft
dinner.description: Spain greatest food product -- Iberian pig (a breed that infiltrates fat into muscle) fed exclusively on acorns in the cork oak dehesa ecosystem, cured in mountain air for 36-48 months. The acorn diet gives the fat a nutty, complex flavor that melts at room temperature. Sliced paper-thin by hand from a jamonero stand.

dinner.name: Tortilla de Bacalao
ingredients: Salt cod (bacalao -- desalted 24-48 hours in changing water)
Onion, garlic, green and red pepper
instructions: Bacalao (salt cod) is the preserved fish of the Spanish interior
The desalting: 24-48 hours in cold water, changing water 3-4 times -- essential
Under-desalted cod is inedibly salty -- this step cannot be rushed
Onion, garlic, pepper sofrito in olive oil
Desalted shredded cod goes into the sofrito
Beaten eggs poured over -- cook like a tortilla, flip to set both sides
The bacalao tortilla is a Basque and Navarran specialty
Spain has 1,000+ different bacalao recipes
dinner.description: Basque and Navarran salt cod omelette -- bacalao desalted over 24-48 hours in changing water, shredded and cooked in sofrito of onion, garlic, and pepper, then bound with beaten eggs and flipped. Salt cod is the mountain food of inland Spain: preserved Atlantic fish that fed interior regions for centuries.

dinner.name: Caldo Gallego
instructions: Caldo gallego is the everyday Galician soup
Grelos: the bitter young turnip tops -- the ingredient that defines Galician cooking
Grelos are bitter, slightly pungent -- they cut through the richness of pork fat
The bitterness of grelos against pork fat and white beans: the Galician flavor principle
Cooked for a long time -- beans soften and broth absorbs pork richness
Galicia is the Celtic region of Spain -- the bagpipes (gaita) play at festivals
dinner.description: Galician everyday soup -- white beans, grelos (bitter young turnip greens, the defining Galician ingredient), salt pork, chorizo, and potatoes. The bitterness of grelos against pork fat is the Galician flavor principle. Rainy, green, Celtic northwestern Spain in a bowl.

dinner.name: Gambas al Ajillo
instructions: Gambas al ajillo is the Spanish tapas institution -- the most ordered tapa
The key technique: everything in the terracotta cazuela at once
The cazuela goes from cold to screaming hot
The garlic must not burn -- slightly golden is correct, dark brown is wrong
The prawns go in when garlic is golden -- they cook in 90 seconds total
The sherry adds steam and deglazes the garlic residue
The terracotta arrives at the table still sizzling
Good crusty bread to mop the garlic oil -- essential
dinner.description: The quintessential Spanish tapa -- large prawns cooked in a sizzling terracotta cazuela with sliced garlic and dried chili in olive oil, deglazed with dry sherry, arrived at the table still bubbling. Good crusty bread for the garlic oil is mandatory. Simple, fast, perfect.

snacks.name: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: Salsa brava: tomatoes, dried red chili, garlic, vinegar
instructions: Patatas bravas is the most iconic Spanish tapa
Bravas = brave or fiery -- from the spicy tomato sauce
The sauce debate: Catalan (alioli only), Madrid (tomato + chili), Valencia (both)
The potato: fried in olive oil -- the interior should be fluffy
The sauce poured over at the table -- not cooked together
snacks.description: The most iconic Spanish tapa -- potatoes cubed and fried in olive oil until crispy-fluffy, dressed with salsa brava (spicy tomato sauce) and/or alioli (garlic mayonnaise). The regional sauce debate: Catalan (alioli), Madrid (tomato-chili), Valencia (both). Served in every Spanish bar.

snacks.name: Croquetas de Jamon
ingredients: Bechamel: butter, flour, whole milk (made thick)
instructions: Croquetas de jamon are Spain most universally loved bar snack
The filling: thick bechamel studded with jamon -- thick enough to shape
Spread onto a tray, cooled completely until firm
Shape into torpedo shapes -- the classic Spanish croqueta
Double-coat: flour, egg, breadcrumbs -- creates the shattering crust
Fry at 180C until deep golden -- outside shatters, inside flows
The inside should be creamy, almost molten -- this is the quality marker
snacks.description: Spain universal bar snack -- thick jamon-studded bechamel cooled until firm, shaped into torpedos, coated in breadcrumbs and fried until the outside shatters to reveal a creamy-molten interior. The inside should flow when broken. Each Spanish grandmother has their recipe.

snacks.name: Aceitunas Alinadas (Marinated Olives)
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, sherry vinegar
instructions: Marinated olives are the first thing on every Spanish bar table
Spain is the world largest olive producer
Manzanilla: the briny green Sevilla olive -- crisp, firm, salty
Arbequina: the small, fruity Catalan olive -- softer, milder
The marinade: garlic, orange peel, cumin, oregano -- warm, fragrant
In Granada: every drink comes with a free tapa including olives
snacks.description: The Spanish bar first course -- green olives marinated with garlic, orange peel, cumin, and oregano in olive oil and sherry vinegar. Spain is the world largest olive producer. In Granada, olives and a free tapa come with every drink ordered.

snacks.name: Sobrasada on Toast with Honey
instructions: Sobrasada is the Mallorcan (Balearic Islands) spreadable raw pork sausage
Made from Mallorcan black pig (porc negre) -- a heritage breed
The sausage is spreadable because it is raw-cured, not cooked
Sweet paprika gives deep red-orange color and sweet smokiness
Honey drizzled over the spread sobrasada: the classic Mallorcan combination
The honey sweetness against the fatty-spicy spread -- the combination is the island
snacks.description: Mallorcan spreadable raw pork sausage -- made from heritage black pig (porc negre), cured with sweet paprika into a soft spreadable texture, served on toast with honey drizzled over. The honey against the fatty-spicy red spread is the Mallorcan combination. PDO-protected.

desserts.name: Crema Catalana
ingredients: Whole milk (not cream -- Catalan, not French)
instructions: Crema catalana is the Catalan predecessor of creme brulee -- the debate with France is ongoing
Key difference: crema catalana uses MILK, not cream -- lighter, less rich
Cinnamon and lemon infused into the milk -- different from vanilla creme brulee
The custard is set on the stovetop (not oven-baked)
The burnt sugar crust: traditionally done with a special iron disk heated in fire
Crema catalana is the dessert of Sant Josep (March 19)
The caramel crust must crack cleanly -- the tap test with the spoon is the ritual
desserts.description: Catalan cinnamon-lemon milk custard with burnt sugar crust -- made with whole milk (not cream: lighter than French creme brulee), cornstarch-set on the stovetop (not oven-baked), infused with cinnamon and lemon peel. The Catalan predecessor of creme brulee -- and Catalonia maintains it came first.

desserts.name: Tarta de Santiago
ingredients: Icing sugar (for the Santiago cross stencil)
instructions: Tarta de Santiago is the Galician almond cake -- the pilgrimage cake
Santiago de Compostela is the endpoint of the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage
The distinctive decoration: the Cross of St James stenciled in icing sugar
The cake: almost entirely ground almonds and eggs -- very little flour
The texture: dense, moist, nutty -- slightly sticky from the almond oil
The cake is gluten-free by nature -- almonds replace flour
Tarta de Santiago with a glass of Albarino: the complete pilgrimage reward
desserts.description: Galician pilgrimage cake -- almost entirely ground almonds and eggs, dense and moist with lemon zest and cinnamon, decorated with the Cross of Santiago stenciled in icing sugar. Sold to pilgrims arriving at Santiago de Compostela cathedral since medieval times. Naturally gluten-free.

desserts.name: Turron (Christmas Nougat)
ingredients: Almonds (whole toasted for Alicante; ground for Jijona)
instructions: Turron is the Christmas sweet of Spain -- eaten exclusively at Christmas
Two classic types: Alicante (hard, with whole almonds) and Jijona (soft, ground almonds)
Turron de Alicante: hard, glassy, honey-amber with whole toasted almonds embedded
Turron de Jijona: soft, paste-like, intensely almond-flavored
Both types have protected denomination (PGI) from their Valencian production towns
Spain produces 35,000+ tons of turron per year for Christmas consumption
The Moorish origin: almonds + honey combination comes from Moorish-era Al-Andalus
Every Spanish Christmas table has turron -- the confectionery of the season
desserts.description: The Spanish Christmas nougat -- Turron de Alicante (hard, glassy with whole toasted almonds) and Turron de Jijona (soft, paste-like, intensely almond) are the two classics, both PGI-protected from their Valencian production towns. Moorish origin: the almonds + honey combination from Al-Andalus survived the Reconquista. Every Spanish Christmas table has turron.

drinks.name: Sangria
instructions: Sangria is the internationally known Spanish drink -- more consumed by tourists than locals
Spanish people drink more cerveza and wine than sangria at home
The wine: Spanish red, not the finest but not the worst
The brandy de Jerez is the Spanish touch -- Jerez brandy has a distinctive character
The citrus juice brings freshness; the sugar balances; the cinnamon gives warmth
Let sit for an hour minimum before serving -- the ingredients need to meld
Tinto de verano (red wine + lemon soda) is what Spaniards actually drink in summer
drinks.description: Spain internationally known summer wine punch -- Spanish red wine with Jerez brandy, citrus juice, fruit slices, cinnamon, and sparkling water over ice. More consumed by tourists than locals. Let it sit an hour for the flavors to meld.

drinks.name: Cava
ingredients: Cava sparkling wine (Catalan -- traditional method from Xarello, Macabeo, Parellada grapes)
instructions: Cava is the Catalan sparkling wine -- made by the traditional (Champagne) method
The grapes: Xarello, Macabeo, Parellada -- indigenous Catalan varieties
Made in the Penedes region of Catalonia
Same technique as Champagne -- at a fraction of the price
Cava is the New Year toast in Spain
The twelve grapes ritual: eating 12 grapes at midnight (one per bell) with cava
This tradition began in 1909 in Alicante -- now universal in Spain
Brut Nature is the driest cava -- no dosage added after disgorgement
drinks.description: Catalan sparkling wine -- traditional method (same as Champagne) from indigenous Xarello, Macabeo, and Parellada grapes in the Penedes region. The New Year toast of Spain. The twelve grapes ritual (one grape per midnight bell) eaten with cava since 1909. Brut Nature is the driest.

drinks.name: Rebujito (Sherry Lemonade)
instructions: Rebujito is the Andalusian festival drink -- the feria drink of Seville and Jerez
Feria: the spring fairs of Andalusia -- specifically the Feria de Abril in Seville
At the feria: thousands of casetas serve rebujito all day and night
The drink: fino sherry + lemon soda, 50/50, over ice
The fino sherry is the key -- its dry, nutty, slightly oxidized character
Diluted with lemon soda: the fino becomes lighter, refreshing, easy to drink
Rebujito is dangerously drinkable for its alcohol content
drinks.description: Andalusian festival drink for the Feria de Abril -- fino sherry and lemon soda 50/50 over ice, served all day and night in the casetas marquees. The fino sherry diluted with lemon soda becomes light, refreshing, and dangerously drinkable. The green-rimmed white cup is the Seville Feria icon.
